title: Range trading

overview.objective: Buy near the bottom of a sideways range and sell near the top.
overview.context: Markets that have tested the same support and resistance several times.

simple.simple: Find a market bouncing between a floor ([[support]]) and a ceiling ([[resistance]]). Buy after price bounces off the floor, aim just below the ceiling, and stop trading the range once price closes outside it.
simple.balanced: Ranges end with a breakout, often after some false ones. Waiting for a close back above support, instead of buying as price falls, avoids some breaks at a worse price. The [[risk-reward-ratio]] is limited by the height of the range.

reasoning: If many traders watch the same levels, price may keep turning near them until something changes. Trading inside those levels with a nearby stop could then have small, defined risk. That is the reasoning, not evidence; ranges end without warning.

rules.label: A simplified educational version, not any trader's system
rules: A range needs at least two touches of support and two of resistance.
Buy only after a candle closes back above support (dips below that close back inside are allowed).
Place the stop 0.5 × ATR below support.
Once a candle closes outside the range, stop trading it until a new range forms. Size for no more than 1% risk.

demo.lookFor: Mark support and resistance where price turned at least twice. Note how close each turn came to the line, and what happened when price finally closed outside.

replay.instructions: Replay the Sideways scenario. Draw the range only after two touches of each side, trade only bounces that close back inside, and stop when a candle closes outside.

exercise.prompt: Which statements are true under the simplified rules? Pick all that apply.
exercise.situation: A fictional commodity in USD (simulated). Support at 85.00 was touched 3 times, resistance at 89.00 twice. The latest candle dipped to 84.80 and closed at 85.30. ATR is 1.20.

options.text: The range has enough touches for the rules
options.explanation: Right: at least two on each side.

options.text: The close back above support is an entry trigger
options.explanation: Right: the candle closed at 85.30, above 85.00.

options.text: A stop 0.5 × ATR below support is at 84.40
The target should be above 89.00, in case it breaks out
options.explanation: No: the target is just below resistance.

options.text: The dip to 84.80 ended the range
options.explanation: No: the rules end the range on a close outside it, and this candle closed inside.

failureAnalysis: A breakout through support hits the stop, sometimes with a gap.
Many touches can mean the level is weakening, not strengthening.
Targets are limited by the range height, so costs take a larger share.
Deciding where the range is involves judgement.
limitations: Touch counts and the 0.5 × ATR stop are examples for learning, not tested values.
No claim is made that ranges hold or that these rules make money.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Support is 1.2600 and resistance 1.2700. A candle closes at 1.2580. What do the rules say?

options.explanation: No: price is outside the range.

options.text: Wait for RSI to fall further
options.explanation: No: RSI is not part of these rules.

options.text: Do not buy: a close outside the range ends it until a new range forms
options.explanation: Right: the rules stop trading the range after a close outside it.
